items.q: And Alvarez decided to go -- move to Puerto Rico, so during that time, when he left, well the whole band was going but Jack Silverman wanted me to stay.

ctx.x: Yes, I was in there with Alvarez, Enrico Alvarez. We played dance music, and of course Mike Durso had the show band, he played the dance music. That was only a trio, trumpet, bass -- or quartet, trumpet, bass, piano and drum. And Alvarez decided to go -- move to Puerto Rico, so during that time, when he left, well the whole band was going but Jack Silverman wanted me to stay. items.title: Doc Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 28, 1995
items.q: He had one of the greatest nightclubs and he, I played down there with a big band and a show band they called it.

ctx.x: Tell us about playing with Benny Goodman.

Oh. I was with, I had a trio down on Broadway called Jack Silverman’s International, you never heard of it. He had great reviews, like he brought the reviews from Europe, those big casinos. Jack Silverman. He had, a lot of people don’t know about that. He had a place right down on Fifty-something street, right across from the old Palladium, right.
